claim: In people, priming independence versus interdependence moves later judgments by a small-to-moderate amount on average (weighted d 0.34, 67 studies, N 6,240; 0.42 without 3 anomalous studies), largest on relationality (0.61) and cognition (0.54), small on values (0.29) and self-concept (0.26).
agent_test: Use d about 0.3 as the planning prior; do not expect a switch.

claim: The meta-analytic average is inflated: trim-and-fill cuts weighted d to 0.17 (24 imputed studies), most studies had no control condition, and meta-analyses average about 3x preregistered replications in general (Kvarven et al., second-hand).
agent_test: Pre-register a minimum effect of interest of about 2 points of accuracy; count a cue only if it beats that at equal tokens.
audit: downgraded 2026-11-10 by check_established.py: only 1 opened source(s) from distinct authors

claim: The best-known lexical prime (pronoun circling and story primes of Gardner et al. 1999) failed a large preregistered replication in China: N 468, F(2,462)=0.283 on self-description, BF01 about 32; the original design was underpowered (5-12% power for the replication effects). Counter-evidence: a pre-registered close digital replication of the pronoun prime in Waterloo students found d .47-.52 on spatial recall among full compliers (N 87) but d .10-.15 with no compliance filter (N 193), so the prime can work when followed.
schema_part: G (do not trust a bare cue)
agent_test: Run a pronoun-style we/I prefix versus no prefix on reasoning items at equal tokens; expect null.

claim: Activity-based primes (solitary versus collective tasks) did not move self-construal or analytic-holistic style in two experiments (N 82 and 132); one of seven measures moved in Exp 2, in the opposite direction and not significant after Bonferroni.
agent_test: Compare a cue of doing a worked sub-task with a cue of a label; do not assume behaviour primes transfer.

claim: Human priming results are task-specific and conditional: the same self-construal prime changed some face tasks and not others, moved only women in a fairness game, worked only in a baseline subgroup, or only under social threat.
agent_test: Report cue effect per item family, never one pooled score.

claim: Prime type matters in the meta-analysis: rich content primes (SDFF d 0.49, scrambled sentence 0.45, Sumerian warrior about 0.45) beat language-as-prime (about 0.1 on values, 0.17 in Asian samples); group imagination was 0.32; priming both relational and group collectivism (0.52) beats one level (0.28-0.39).
agent_test: Compare a task-reflection cue (what do I share with the people affected) versus a language switch versus a label.

claim: A one-line country persona cue reduces distance to survey values for 71-81% of 107 countries in GPT-class models (GPT-4o 2.42 to 1.57), and the effect replicates in five open-weight models (e.g. llama3.3 2.217 to 0.973).
schema_part: O (frame switch by cue), values only
agent_test: Persona cue versus none on a held-out value survey, equal tokens.

claim: Persona cues fail or backfire for 19-29% of targets (GPT-4o Taiwan 2.40 to 3.94, Finland 0.20 to 2.43; Llama 3.1 worse by total distance; France worse in Luther and Brown), and gains are model-specific and larger for stronger models. Item-level analogue: with a role persona on AQuA, 15.75% of items turned right and 13.78% turned wrong (Coin Flip 4.00% vs 18.00%).
agent_test: Add a check step that measures the shift against a reference and reverts if worse.

claim: Persona cues give stereotypes rather than calibrated profiles: models rate the US individualist and Japan collectivist regardless of real Hofstede scores; only one model-method cell correlated (r 0.71); a cue is partly obeyed as deference to a claimed identity.
agent_test: Give a false identity claim; check whether style follows the claim regardless of task evidence.

claim: Prompt language as an orientation cue is weak and unstable in current LLMs: Lu et al. found holistic/interdependent shifts, but an 8-model, 960-observation replication found language d 0.045, only qwen d 0.54, signs mixed; two other studies find mostly null or reversed language effects.
agent_test: Do not use a language switch as a scaffold lever; test only with many items and models.

claim: Explicit task framing steers LLM output far more than a culture label: change-framed versus neutral prompts gave |d| about 2.1 (eta-squared 0.54) across all 8 models, whereas language gave d 0.045. This is partly a demand effect.
agent_test: Compare an explicit consider-what-may-change instruction with a culture cue on the same items; check for demand.

claim: Reasoning-first cues beat bare personas modestly: Anthropological Prompting raised soft similarity 0.4834 to 0.5102 and hard 0.2443 to 0.2838 (Egypt, GPT-3.5); DSPy-optimized cues sometimes beat manual cues (llama4 2.006 to 0.818) but not on every model.
agent_test: Persona-only versus emic/etic-then-answer cue, equal tokens, multiple models.

claim: Default LLM style is mixed, not blank: GPT-3.5/4 read holistic on process scales (triadic categorization 0.85-0.87, AHS 5.01-5.35 versus human 4.87) and independent on self-construal scales; an RLHF persona can swamp cues.
agent_test: Measure the agent's baseline style on a fixed battery before any cue.

claim: Self-report change does not imply behaviour change: small-model Singelis scores did not predict behaviour in multi-turn scenarios (blog pilot); in humans a prime can be delivered (92.7% correct word counts) with no downstream change.
agent_test: Score the task answer, not the model's description of its own style.

claim: Output material interacts with the cue: holistic share of VLM captions rose from 26.10% to 73.37% with Japanese images, so language, content and model are tangled.
agent_test: Hold items fixed and vary only the cue.

claim: No LLM study found varies a human-style priming task (SDFF, pronoun circling, warrior story) ahead of a reasoning benchmark and measures accuracy; the literature tests persona or language on values or style readouts. Gap pass confirmed the absence in Crossref (weak: other search APIs were rate-limited); role-persona prefix studies exist (162 roles, 2,410 questions: no mean gain) but none use an orientation prime.
agent_test: First direct test: SDFF-style prefix versus pronoun prefix versus none on a reasoning set, equal tokens.

claim: Compliance gates the human pronoun-prime effect: in a pre-registered replication of Kuhnen and Oyserman Study 2 the effect was d .47-.52 (N 87, full compliers), d .26-.30 (N about 157, partial) and d .10-.15 (N 193, no filter, all p>.25). The cut-off was not pre-registered. Pooled close replications: d .35 (three labs).
schema_part: G (verify uptake before crediting a cue)
agent_test: Log whether the model's output obeys the cue (e.g. names the relations or the parts asked for) and report the cue effect for obeying and non-obeying runs separately, with the unfiltered number as primary.

claim: Role or persona prefixes do not raise average accuracy on factual or reasoning items when tested widely (162 roles, 4 model families, 2,410 questions: no gain over no persona), and vary by model and task (llama3-8B worse on 7 of 12 sets; GPT-4 up on Coin Flip 66.93 to 75.93).
agent_test: Treat any orientation prefix as zero-effect until a per-model panel shows otherwise.
audit: downgraded 2026-11-10 by check_established.py: only 1 opened source(s) from distinct authors

claim: A choose-between step recovers part of persona backfire: comparing persona and neutral answers with a position-bias-free judge raised average accuracy over persona alone (GPT-4 six arithmetic sets 92.28 to 93.15; llama3-8B 82.32 to 84.23, and 74.49 to 76.38 on the other six sets where persona alone was below base).
schema_part: G + O (check against reference, revert if worse)
agent_test: Run cued and neutral answer, let a second pass pick, compare with the better single arm at matched calls.

claim: Sycophancy to a claimed identity as the cause of persona-cue gains is plausible (assistants favour answers matching user views; warm-tuned models validate false beliefs 10-30 points more) but untested: no source compared an identity cue with an identity-free task cue on orientation items.
agent_test: Three arms on holistic items: 'you are a Chinese person', 'consider relations and change', and a neutral control, scored on answers, with the third-party view check.

claim: Baseline orientation differs by model (DeepSeek downplays self-enhancement relative to ChatGPT and Gemini), but no source tested whether the baseline moderates cue effect in LLMs as it did in humans (Jiang and Sui). Gaps 2, 3, 9 and 10 remain open; Lu et al. full text was paywalled.
agent_test: Measure each model's baseline on a fixed holistic-analytic item set before the cue panel and regress cue gain on baseline.
